2609.07943.title: Beliefs and Behavior in Language Models
2609.07943.paper_summary: There is significant uncertainty about whether abstractions like beliefs or desires usefully describe the behavior of large language models (LLMs). In addition to the inherent scientific interest of this question, these latent quantities are often invoked to explain the behavior of LLMs to users or to define and evaluate harmful behaviors which are relative to intent. Nevertheless, we currently lack a means to systematically test whether concepts like "belief" are well-applied to LLMs, and hence whether they are likely to be fruitful ingredients of attempts to align models with human interests. We propose an approach for empirically studying such questions, asking whether a single latent variable inferred from the LLMs' outputs -- interpreted as a degree of belief -- allows an observer to make interpretable predictions of how the LLMs' will respond to new prompts. We find that highly capable models are usefully described as holding beliefs and that, generally, the predictability of model outputs based on an inferred latent belief tracks overall trends in model capability. Building on these findings, we provide empirical strategies to study how beliefs in LLMs can be measured, the extent to which LLMs comply with instructed decision rules or payoffs, and how beliefs evolve within individual instances of an LLM over the course of reasoning.
2609.07943.paper_summary_zh: 對於像信念或欲望這樣的抽象概念是否能有效描述大型語言模型（LLMs）的行為，存在著顯著的不確定性。除了這個問題本身固有的科學興趣外，這些潛在量通常被用來解釋 LLMs 對用戶的行為，或定義和評估相對於意圖的有害行為。儘管如此，我們目前缺乏系統性測試「信念」等概念是否適用於 LLMs 的方法，因此也無法判斷它們是否可能成為使模型與人類利益對齊的有益成分。我們提出了一種實證研究這些問題的方法，詢問從 LLMs 的輸出中推斷的單一潛在變量——解釋為信念的程度——是否能讓觀察者對 LLMs 對新提示的反應做出可解釋的預測。我們發現，高能力的模型可以有效地描述為持有信念，並且通常，基於推斷的潛在信念的模型輸出可預測性與模型能力的整體趨勢相符。在這些發現的基礎上，我們提供了實證策略來研究 LLMs 中信念的測量方法、LLMs 遵循指示的決策規則或報酬的程度，以及信念在 LLM 的個別實例中在推理過程中的演變。
